title: Towards end-to-end automation of AI research
abstract: The automation of science is a long-standing ambition in artificial intelligence (AI) research. We introduce The AI Scientist, the first comprehensive system for fully automated scientific discovery, enabling Large Language Model (LLM) agents to perform research independently, from ideation, writing code, running experiments, visualizing results, and authoring full scientific papers in LaTeX, to automated peer review.

title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
abstract: Scientific discovery is driven by scientists generating hypotheses for complex problems that undergo rigorous experimental validation. To augment this process, we introduce Co-Scientist, a multi-agent AI system that synthesizes literature, formulates research hypotheses, designs validation protocols, and generates automated research write-ups.

title: SciAgents: Automating Scientific Discovery Through Bioinspired Multi-Agent Intelligent Graph Reasoning
abstract: A key challenge in AI is the creation of systems capable of autonomously advancing scientific understanding. We present SciAgents, a multi-agent system utilizing large-scale ontological knowledge graphs to autonomously uncover hidden patterns, generate novel interdisciplinary hypotheses, design validation experiments, and draft scientific manuscripts.

title: Agent Laboratory: Using LLM Agents as Research Assistants
abstract: Historically, scientific discovery demands substantial time and resources from initial conception to final results. We introduce Agent Laboratory, an autonomous multi-agent research framework where specialized agents (PhD student, Postdoc, Professor) collaborate across three phases: literature review, experimentation, and full-length scientific paper writing in LaTeX.

title: PaperOrchestrator: An LLM-Orchestrated multi-agent pipeline for automated end-to-end scientific paper writing
source: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
abstract: Academic paper writing is a demanding component of the scientific research workflow. We propose PaperOrchestrator, an LLM multi-agent pipeline tailored for automated end-to-end scientific paper writing, orchestrating outline generation, section drafting, citation verification, and iterative revision to produce rigorous academic papers.

title: PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing
abstract: Synthesizing unstructured research materials into manuscripts is an essential yet under-explored challenge in AI-driven scientific discovery. We introduce PaperOrchestra, a modular multi-agent framework comprising planners, section writers, citation auditors, and reviewer agents that collaboratively compose high-depth research manuscripts.

title: ResearchAgent: Iterative Research Idea Generation over Scientific Literature with Large Language Models
abstract: We propose ResearchAgent, an LLM-powered agent that iteratively generates novel research ideas over scientific publications by constructing core entity graphs and validating concepts. Augmented with multiple reviewing agents providing peer feedback, ResearchAgent iteratively refines research proposals and draft manuscripts.

title: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
abstract: We introduce The AI Scientist-v2, an end-to-end agentic system capable of producing entirely AI-generated peer-review-accepted workshop papers. By integrating agentic tree search into the ideation, coding, and paper-writing pipeline, the system dramatically improves argumentation, background literature coverage, and manuscript quality.

title: From Automation to Autonomy: A Survey on Large Language Models in Scientific Discovery
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are catalyzing a paradigm shift in scientific discovery, evolving from passive tools into autonomous research agents. This survey presents a comprehensive overview of multi-agent architectures in literature retrieval, automated hypothesis generation, and end-to-end scientific paper writing.

title: A review of large language models and autonomous agents in chemistry
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as powerful tools across scientific disciplines. This review highlights LLM capabilities and autonomous agents (such as PaperQA and ChemCrow) performing scientific tasks including academic paper scraping, literature synthesis, experimental planning, and automated manuscript drafting.
